clue.text: Coppers ordered to West End scene

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of the word coppers are put into a new arrangement
End points to the final letter of the word West just before it

explanation.surface: Police officers are sent to a scene in London's theatreland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' gives an anagram of the police word and 'End' takes one letter of West. 'West End' reads as London's theatre district but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide view of landscape, the same as a scene laid out before the eye.

clue.text: Spring made by quiet predator

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
an ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A silent hunter leaps out.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce is the snow leopard; P is the musical mark for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to spring suddenly onto prey.

clue.text: Exceptional child very likely to, succeed

parts.note: odd means unusual or exceptional
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A gifted child is a good bet for success.
explanation.definitionFit: An odds-on favourite is so strongly fancied that the betting is less than evens.

clue.text: Possibly fish can change course

annotationWithheld.why: Possibly fish can change course (9): PERCH plus an anagram of CAN gives only eight letters; no word in the clue honestly supplies the E of PERCHANCE, and no source found gives the parse

clue.text: Opposing sides in matches

parts.note: counter means opposing, as in counter-argument
parts are sides, as in taking someone's part

explanation.surface: Rival teams in sporting fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' reads as games, but it is the definition: things that match one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterparts are equivalents, people or things that correspond to each other.

clue.text: Owned up about king backing segregation for women

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the whole assembled string from right to left
about means the first pieces go around the letter for king

parts.note: owned means had
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone confessed to a monarch's support for keeping women apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the king inside the first two pieces, making HADRUP, and 'backing' turns that whole string round.
explanation.definitionFit: Purdah is the custom in parts of South Asia of screening women from men and strangers.

clue.text: Upstart wise to get employment

parts.note: the start of the word up is its first letter, U
sage means wise

explanation.surface: A newcomer with brains finds a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstart' is read as two words: the start of up.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the act of using something, its employment or use.

clue.text: Oppressive in shade, spot I chose

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tyrannical decision made over where to sit in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through shaDE SPOT I Chose; the scan shows the 'I' the held clue dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Despotic means ruling like a tyrant, cruel and domineering.

clue.text: Order for NE that is uncertain

indicators.note: order for asks for the letters of NE that is to be arranged afresh

explanation.surface: An instruction for the north-east region is unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order for' rearranges NE THAT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant means wavering or doubtful.

clue.text: Charged less in this joint

explanation.surface: A butcher's cheaper price on a particular cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To undercut is to sell for less than a rival; the undercut is also the tenderloin cut of beef from under the ribs.

clue.text: Rock python's catching partners in this state

indicators.note: catching means the snake's name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Kaa is the rock python in Kipling's Jungle Book; with the possessive it gives KAAS
North and South are partners at the bridge table, NS

explanation.surface: A big snake wraps round a pair of companions somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Kaa is the rock python in Kipling's Jungle Book; in bridge, North and South play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Business has little capital raised for plant

parts.note: trade means business or commerce
scant means little or barely enough

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the piece is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, as does capital; read with I for one, AI

explanation.surface: A firm with little money behind it puts up a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AI to IA. A1, first-class, is written with letter I for 1; capital also means excellent. 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradescantia is a genus of trailing houseplants, also called spiderwort.

clue.text: Many reluctant to follow churchmen

definitions.note: plural here, while the answer is a collective noun for the clergy as a body

indicators.note: to follow means the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
loth is an old spelling of loath, meaning reluctant

explanation.surface: Lots of people are unwilling to go along with clergymen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts LOTH after C. Many as C (a hundred) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is an idiom for the clergy collectively, from their distinctive dress.

clue.text: Paraded to be dismissed

explanation.surface: Troops on parade face being sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers turned out are paraded for inspection; someone turned out has been evicted or sent away.

clue.text: Basic instruction in the exchange of identities

explanation.surface: A first lesson in swapping who people are.
explanation.definitionFit: An introductory course gives the basics of a subject; introducing strangers is telling each the other's name.

clue.text: Head may come to teach, if in trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of teach if in are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: The principal may arrive to teach if things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges TEACH IF IN. Head looks like a head teacher, but it means a clan leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the leader of a clan or tribe.

clue.text: Sturdy group of thieves?

explanation.surface: A strong gang of robbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading plays on 'thick as thieves': a set of thieves would be a thick set.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset means stocky and solidly built; a set of close friends is thick, as in 'thick as thieves'.

clue.text: Many dollars on Continent — that was Rome for Poe

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand dollars
EUR is the abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: Lots of American money in Europe recalls a poet's line about ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe's 'To Helen' speaks of 'the glory that was Greece, and the grandeur that was Rome'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's line credits Rome with splendour and magnificence.

clue.text: Possession of good seat for MP — has no heirs, oddly

indicators.note: oddly signals that the letters of MP has no heirs appear in a strange order

explanation.surface: A politician with no children is worried about keeping his parliamentary seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges MP HAS NO HEIRS. The seat is not in Parliament but on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A good seat is a rider's balanced position in the saddle, the core of riding skill.

clue.text: It's a disgrace to become drunk

parts.note: a blot on one's name is a disgrace

explanation.surface: Getting drunk brings shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Money raised used in production of cheese

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word for money is written upwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: Cash put up for a cheese-making venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TENNER upside down in the grid. A tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is an enzyme preparation that curdles milk, the start of most cheese-making.

clue.text: Associations attached to group in spy organization

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the agency's initials

parts.note: the CIA is America's Central Intelligence Agency
on can mean attached to, as a lid is on a jar
a sort is a group or kind

explanation.surface: Organisations linked to a cell inside an intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: The CIA, America's Central Intelligence Agency, is the spy organization that goes round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia, plural of consortium, are business partnerships or alliances.

clue.text: Bribed 19? Well, yes

explanation.surface: Paid off and drunk? Certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well, yes' nods to 'well oiled', drunk; 19 refers to the drunk answer at 19-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To oil palms is to bribe; oiled, or well oiled, is slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: Invalid lying thus

explanation.surface: A sick person is not telling the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: An invalid argument is unsound, not true; a lying statement is untrue.

clue.text: Fair Maid of Perth?

parts.note: Scott's novel title, but the Perth meant is in Western Australia, where a pretty young woman has a slang name

explanation.walkthrough: The Fair Maid of Perth is a Walter Scott novel set in Scotland; the question mark sends you to Perth, Australia, and Australian slang for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a young woman, so a fair maid from an Australian city.

clue.text: Confine to stop being crooked, say

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase before it is matched by its pronunciation only

parts.note: to stop being bent means to straighten, which is pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: Lock someone up to stop them being dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a soundalike. Crooked looks like dishonest, but it means bent, as a line is.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to restrict or narrow, so to hem in.

clue.text: Turkish leader introduces Muslim edict in angry speech

indicators.note: leader picks out the opening letter of the word Turkish

parts.note: an irade was a written decree of the Ottoman Sultan

explanation.surface: The head of Turkey brings in a religious decree during a furious outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives T, which goes before IRADE, a decree issued by an Ottoman sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long, furious harangue.

clue.text: Croatian revolutionary in Ulster

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests the letters of Croatian are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A Croatian rebel turns up in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges CROATIAN. Ulster is not the province here but a long heavy overcoat named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long, loose overcoat, a kind of outer garment worn against the weather.
